- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.
- In low-sentiment environments (e.g., sentiment < 0.0), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows to account for volatility.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate upward momentum; cap forecast growth at 2–3% above recent trend.
- Model consistently underestimates true price range in early 30-day horizons; apply a 1–2% upward bias to initial forecast values if sentiment is stable or mildly bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust quickly; introduce a 3–5 day lag correction by reducing forecast slope by 10–15% after sentiment dip.
